sense: a number of things one after another

terms.gloss: a series, a sequence, a chain
terms.comment: Of a chain of events or ideas from Cicero on; of things in a row mostly post-classical (Lewis & Short). No genitive or dative is found (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a row, a series in order
terms.comment: Things in turn are ōrdine, one after the other.

phrases.latin: innumerābilis annōrum seriēs et fuga temporum
phrases.english: the countless series of the years, and the flight of time

phrases.latin: est enim admīrābilis quaedam continuātiō seriēsque rērum, ut alia ex aliā nexa et omnēs inter sē aptae conligātaeque videantur
phrases.english: for there is a wonderful continuity and sequence in the subject, each part linked to the next and all of them fitted and bound together

sources: Lewis & Short: series · Lewis & Short: ordo
Cicero’s De natura deorum and De divinatione, and Horace’s Odes, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
